title: scheduler: transparent hedge-window coordinator for continuous batcher fairness and starvation mitigation
author: Ravi Patel
release_notes: Introduces a hedge-window coordinator to reduce starvation and tail latency in continuous batching. Adds new scheduler knobs (hedge_window_ms, starvation_threshold_ms) and observability for queue fairness. Backwards compatible; opt-in via config.
description: Motivation: under mixed workloads with a small fraction of KV-heavy, long-sequence requests we see persistent starvation of short, latency-sensitive requests in the continuous batcher. Existing hedging was coarse and generated microbursts that destabilized puddled queues. This change implements a transparent 'hedge-window coordinator' that provides softer, aligned hedges and drain windows per admission cohort to improve fairness while avoiding batch fragmentation. || Summary of changes: 1) runtime/scheduler/hedge_window_coordinator.go: new coordinator implementing aligned hedges and soft drain windows; exposes knobs hedge_window_ms, min_drain_tokens, starvation_threshold_ms. 2) runtime/scheduler/queue_instrumentation.go: per-cohort queuing metrics (queued_time_histogram, starvation_signals). 3) runtime/kv/cache_hints.go: probe hedges set a lightweight KV-prefetch hint to reduce cache cold-starts for hedged requests. 4) runtime/kernels/hint_selector.go: small change to prioritize low-seq kernels for cohorts with high short-request fraction. 5) docs/scheduler/hedge-window.md: operator guide and tuning recommendations. 6) test/bench/kv_fairness_bench.yml and test/scheduler/hedge_window_test.go: microbench + property tests. 7) examples/bench/kv-heavy.yml: benchmark configs used for validation. || Commits (high level): - Add coordinator and config parsing - Wire metrics & kernel hinting - Add tests and bench harness - Fix race on cohort state flush - Add docs and operator guidance - Address review feedback: tighten default hedge_window_ms -> 8ms, add new metric queue_starvation_rate || Rationale: the coordinator groups hedges into short windows that aim to (a) give short requests a predictable service opportunity (b) limit hedging concurrency to avoid burst amplification and (c) signal starvation to allow backlog-aware admission throttles to kick in. Probe hedges will opportunistically trigger KV prefetch hints for anticipated cache misses which reduces hedged-request tail. Kernel hinting steers tiny sequences to the faster attention kernels to keep hedges cheap. || Benchmarks: microbench on 8xA100 cluster with mixed workload (5% long KV sequences at 4x tokens): 95th latency for short requests dropped 18% relative to trunk; p99 improved 12%. Tail improvement persisted across sequence length distributions. Throughput delta: -0.6% (within noise). Cost impact: negligible; average token utilization unchanged. || Review conversation summary: Maya Chen: "Nice approach, provides a softer hedge vs full replicate hedging. Please add more instrumentation for hedged vs normal kernel selection."; Author: "added hedged_kernel_choice metric and exposed it in the coordinator." Evan Brooks: "Concern about interplay with autoscaler and Dedicated capacity; can hedges cause transients?"; Author: "added min_drain_tokens guard and expanded bench to include autoscaler spike scenario; results show stable behavior with default knobs." Lina Gomez: "Race on cohort state seen in initial tests."; Author: "fixed with atomic cohort state updates and added unit test." Approvals: Maya and Lina approved after fixes; Evan gave conditional approval and followed up with a later perf check on staging. || CI: unit tests and bench smoke passed on first run; flaky integration test scheduling/queue_rebalance retried once and passed. Lint and staticcheck green. Perf job ran and uploaded artifact 'hedge-window-perf-20241112' with raw results. || Upgrade notes: opt-in via config.scheduler.hedge_window.enabled (default true for Canary and Dedicated; false for Hosted until staged rollout). Default knobs tuned conservatively. Operators should monitor new metrics queue_starvation_rate and hedged_kernel_choice while rolling out. || Files changed (high level): runtime/scheduler/hedge_window_coordinator.go, runtime/scheduler/hedge_window_test.go, runtime/scheduler/queue_instrumentation.go, runtime/kv/cache_hints.go, runtime/kernels/hint_selector.go, docs/scheduler/hedge-window.md, test/bench/kv_fairness_bench.yml, examples/bench/kv-heavy.yml, go.mod (module deps for bench harness). || Merge: squash and merge to main. Backports: cherrypick candidate for release/2024.12 if canary metrics are positive. || Notes for maintainers: default hedge_window_ms=8ms, starvation_threshold_ms=120ms, min_drain_tokens=4. Consider adjusting hedge_window proportional to observed mean batch latency for workloads with very small token footprints. The coordinator is designed to be low-overhead; metric overhead kept minimal with sampled histograms. If regressions observed, set config.scheduler.hedge_window.enabled=false to revert quickly.
